headline: Markets turn cautious again ahead of Nvidia earnings and Anthropic's debut
body: Futures opened the week lower, with Nasdaq 100 contracts down roughly 0.8% and S&P 500 futures off about 0.3%, as tech led declines and European and Asian markets also softened. That pullback comes right after a sharp snapback: the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq each logged their biggest weekly gain since August last week, clawing back a meaningful chunk of the AI-valuation-driven rout from November 5, a session that pushed the Nasdaq into correction territory and sent the VIX up roughly 70% in a single day to the high-20s. CNN's Fear & Greed gauge touched Extreme Fear, near 20, during that stretch. Today's softer open reads less like renewed panic and more like the bounce pausing to re-test its footing before the week's catalysts hit.

Those catalysts are substantial. Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results tomorrow after the close, a report now carrying outsized weight as the next referendum on whether AI capital spending and chip demand justify current valuations after two weeks of violent swings in the group. Layered on top, Anthropic is pushing toward a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT, targeting a valuation near $1.4 trillion with shares indicated around $70-78, a debut that could land within days and double as its own test of risk appetite. Retail and social-media chatter was too thin and dated to read as a clear signal today, so this take leans on price action and positioning around these two events rather than invented crowd-sentiment specifics.
